_readme: THE DEMO SET: plans a visitor may open on any box, ours and only ours.
THE DEMO TAB IS THIS FILE. /api/demo-plans answers from here alone, so
the tab shows exactly these plans, one card each, on a box holding zero
jobs for them or sixty-three. It is NOT built from job rows any more:
that showed the box's history (a dozen or more jobs for one sheet) and
every one of them carried a detection computed weeks ago, which is a
pre-warmed cache presented as a live run.
AND THEY OPEN FRESH. POST /api/demo/{name}/open sweeps everything
derived from the PDF before handing it over, so a visitor always meets
an UNDETECTED document and presses Detect themselves. One job per plan
is reused for that, so opening a demo three times does not grow the
registry by three rows - see server.py _demo_job.
One source of truth, read by four things:
server.py       /api/demo-plans renders the cards from this file;
/api/demo/{name}/open opens one fresh; and a job row
is still flagged demo:true when its display name is a
key below AND the row is owner-less (the existing
shared/owner visibility rule - a client upload that
happens to carry the same filename is NEVER a demo),
which is what keeps demo jobs off Your projects.
webui/app.js    draws the Demo tab from /api/demo-plans; a plan whose
PDF is not on this box still gets a card, saying so.
seed-demo.sh    uploads these onto a hosted box, and refuses to run if
it does not seed every name here. Any pre-detection it
does is swept by the first demo open, by design.
provision_demo.py  --rewrite-owners keeps an OWNER-LESS row wearing one
of these names (or a shared_names name) shared while
it moves the other owner-less rows to staff; a row that
has an owner is never touched, whatever it is named.
WHO SEES A SHARED ROW (2026-10-01). An owner-less row is open to every
account ONLY when its display name is a key below or one of
`shared_names` (exactly; case does not matter). Any other owner-less row - a card that was removed
from this file, a sheet seeded under an older manifest - is STAFF-ONLY
(server.py _shared_for_all). It is hidden, never deleted. So shrinking
this file takes a card off every client's screen with no server step.
`shared_names`: the sheets of the two shared plan sets (the Loves Lane
civil sheets and Belle Farms) as they are named on a seeded store, from
this file's history and provision_demo.py's old prefixes. Some are
shared but are not demo cards; these names keep those open to everyone.
EXACT names, not prefixes: a prefix let an owner-less "C4.0-SITE-GRADING-
PLAN for <someone>.pdf" open for every account (critic bid-content-1,
RISK-3).
The key is the DISPLAY name, which is the filename with our own
upload_<hash>_ prefix stripped (server.py _display_name). That is what
makes one list work for a laptop that opened the file by path and for a
hosted box that received it through /api/upload.
PROVENANCE RULE, not negotiable: only the two shared plan sets (the
Loves Lane civil sheets and Belle Farms) may appear here. Every other
set in the corpus or in the client folders is a client's drawing and
staff-only, and eighteen accounts on the box compete with each other.
tests/test_projects_api.py and tests/test_demo_seed.py enforce this.
`page` is the sheet a visitor should land on (engine page index, 0-based
- printed sheet number is page+1 on these sets).
`shows` is printed on the card. EVERY ONE OF THESE LINES WAS WRITTEN
FROM A LIVE RUN ON THAT SHEET, not from what a sheet of its type usually
carries. Re-measured 2026-10-02 on the 2.0 build (out/verify/2026-10-02/
demo-cards/): the 2026-08-31 lines carried counts the engine no longer
gives (1,429 runs / 113 styles where the page says 1402 / 109) and
promises the page does not keep (a door count that shows nowhere, a
scale it "refuses to pick" where it picks one and warns). So: NO EXACT
COUNTS on a card - they go stale with every engine change. If
you add a plan, open it and detect it first, and describe what actually
came out. A card that promises a capability the sheet does not exercise
is the one thing a demo set must never do.
REMOVED 2026-10-01 (owner's decision): every card that was not from the
two shared sets - the substation civils, the stair-plan grading sheet,
the house set, the residential construction set and the two
commercial addenda sheets. They were other parties' drawings.
DROPPED earlier after testing: window_takeoff_benchmark_plan.pdf - our
synthetic fixture, not a drawing. It stays in the corpus as a test bed.
shared_names: Belle Farms Upper Parcel ROAD GRADING 1 of 2.pdf
Belle Farms Upper Parcel ROAD GRADING 2 of 2.pdf

C4.0-SITE-GRADING-PLAN-Rev.1.pdf.shows: A busy site grading sheet: more than a thousand lines in over a hundred styles, each carrying the drafter's own layer name.

Belle Farms Structural Plans.pdf.shows: A building floor plan. Pick rooms fills a room with one click. Some printed dimensions do not match the scale, and the app flags it.

Belle Farms Upper Parcel ROAD GRADING 1.shows: Heavy topography on a road grading sheet. It prints three scales. The app shows all three and tells you to set the one for your drawing.

C6.0-WATER-MAIN-PLAN-AND-PROFILE-Rev.1.p.shows: Wet utilities, plan and profile on one page — water, gas and electric runs above, the profile band below.

C8.0-STORM-LAYOUT-Rev.1.pdf.shows: A storm drain layout with O-PIPE runs. Its scale caption had to be read by OCR, and the drawn scale bar confirms the reading: 20 ft to the inch both ways.
